utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really don't know that I ever mentioned military facilities. I just know that there are no military facilities where we are; I mean, in my neighbourhood. As for further away from me, I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I don't think you're going to get much further with this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no more questions then.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, please, the Chamber is here to establish whether your house was actually shelled and then to determine the responsibility for this shelling; and to establish the responsibility of this, we need to know where the shell came from, this shell that fell on your house, and maybe you could help us. In your statement dated May 17, 2006, you say on paragraph 3 that "Zuc hill was behind us." I'm quoting here: "Zuc hill was behind us." I will read it in English. "[In English] Zuc hill was behind us, and the high ground across the river to the south was occupied by our troops so that there was no sniper fire coming into our neighbourhood." [Interpretation] End of quote. So here we have the location of Zuc hill in relation to the ABiH troops. Then if we go to your second statement, you say in that second statement of March 12th, 1997, at the last paragraph you say, and I quote again in English: "[In English] I don't know myself from which direction the projectile came, but I was told that it came from Hresa." [Interpretation] My question is the following: Of course, we don't have a map in front of us right now, and maybe the exercise will be a bit difficult, but please do your best do tell us the location of your house compared to Hresa and in relation to Zuc hill, because this could possibly help us determine where the shell actually came from, in relation to your house, to the ABiH troops, and to the troops of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: ANDJA GOTOVAC
utterances.text: I don't know how I'm going to interpret this; I mean, about our street. Alipasino Polje is what it is called, but we are on the road to Rajlovac; I mean, the street is. Somebody says from Hresa and other people say from Trebevic. I don't know from where it came from. I'm not sure where it came from. On that day, in the morning, there was absolutely no shooting between 9.30 and 10.00. I heard, or rather, I thought that it was an aeroplane flying low, and at that moment there was an explosion. It was terrible. Things were flying all over the place. There were two people killed, three of us were wounded, a person who lost his leg. I mean, I really don't know how to explain this to you, how to interpret this for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, in relation to your house that was shelled, Hresa, this Hresa neighbourhood, could you tell us if it is north of your house or east or west or south? That is my question. And could you also tell us the distance between Hresa and your house, if you know it?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA GOTOVAC
utterances.text: Believe me that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Witness. So now I would like to ask a question to the Prosecution. I don't know if we will have any further evidence to help us with this incident, at least to establish where the shots came from, where the shell came from, because here we were helpless.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour, yes, we are going to be calling a witness. I understand it's a police investigator that would provide more evidence about the origin or the direction of fire. However, I will also underline that the Prosecution's theory is that only the SRK possessed modified air bombs. That is also part of our theory in terms of proving the origin of fire. But we are bringing witness to give evidence on the origin of fire for this incident and all other air bomb incidents, include also the expert evidence, Berko Zevevic, who will provide technical evidence with respect to the origin of fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, a map has been provided to the Bench. And I would be grateful if could you just quickly by indicating the coordinates tell us approximately where the victim's house was located.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was actually going to ask a question of the witness, in order to provide with you an indication as to where the -- her house was -- is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Then please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: I understand she was difficulty in reading a map so that's why wasn't showing it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Right. But could you help with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mrs. Gotovac, can I just ask you one question. The place where you live, how far away is it from the TV tower -- TV building in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA GOTOVAC
utterances.text: I'm across the road from it. The TV building and my house are on a single line, only I'm in one street and they are in another street.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: So is that about 100 metres or less, or more than 100 metres away?

utterances.speaker: ANDJA GOTOVAC
utterances.text: As the crow flies, maybe it's 100 or 150 metres, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, does that assist you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes. At least it gives me the gist of the neighbourhood and where on the map would be -- what is the direction on the map towards Hrasna, towards the presumed origin of fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Well, in the indictment, the origin of fire is Lukavica; and therefore from her residence, it would be south-west, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is just a suggestion I would like it make. We mentioned Hresa in the statement, perhaps the Prosecutor could indicate to us also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Indicate what?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the Prosecutor mentioned Lukavica and said that was to the south-west in the direction of fire, and Judge Mindua also put a question and mentioned Hresa. So perhaps the Prosecutor could help all and everyone here. Let me remind you that this incident was one of the purposes of our visit, where we had our on-site visit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What is the Prosecutor to help, by doing what? The Prosecutor is not a witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Put the question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Would you like to put that question then?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President, if you're instructing me to, then of course I will. On the other hand, the statement is quite clear that she herself said that she didn't know where the projectile came from, so I didn't see it necessary to ask her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, that concludes your evidence. We thank you for giving it and you may now leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: In view of the fact that there are no further evidence to be given today by witnesses, we will adjourn until tomorrow --

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Do you have another --

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: No, not a witness, unfortunately, but I have a brief application to make pursuant to Rule 75. The Prosecution is calling a witness, it is witness 13, via videolink, and I have been told that he has requested protective measures; in other words, image distortion and pseudonym. I have discussed this with my learned friend, and she has told me there are no objections. The reason to grant a under Rule 75 are that the witness currently resides in Ilidza, and Ilidza is -- he lives with Bosnian Serbs in his neighbourhood, and Bosnian Serbs are frequently returning to that part of Sarajevo. And he is an elderly man, and he just feels for his safety and would not like to be recognised as someone who has given testimony in this trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We grant it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.
